props.title: Wild Reeds
props.initialSlug: Coming-of-age in 1960s France tests four teens

sections.content: Wild Reeds (1994) stands as André Téchiné's masterful coming-of-age drama set against the backdrop of the Algerian War. The film captures the sexual and political awakening of four teenagers in rural France, with François discovering his homosexuality while his friend Maïté grapples with her communist beliefs. Téchiné's approach echoes the raw emotional honesty of Maurice Pialat's work in À nos amours (1983), while presaging the complex sexual politics later explored in Call Me By Your Name (2017). The film's delicate handling of adolescent sexuality influenced later French classics like Water Lilies (2007).

sections.content: Téchiné's film belongs to a rich tradition of French coming-of-age dramas that explore sexuality with remarkable frankness. The Dreamlife of Angels (1998) shares its sensitive portrayal of working-class youth, while Blue Is the Warmest Color (2013) follows its thread of sexual self-discovery. The political backdrop of the Algerian War provides crucial context, similar to how The Last Metro (1980) used WWII to frame its character development.

The film's boarding school setting creates a pressure cooker for adolescent desires, reminiscent of Zero for Conduct (1933) and If.... (1968). However, Téchiné eschews their rebellious anger for a more nuanced exploration of emotional awakening. The character of Henri, the pied-noir student, adds layers of political complexity that echo through later films like Games of Love and Chance (2003). SUBHEAD: French New Wave Influences and Legacy

sections.content: While not strictly part of the French New Wave, Wild Reeds carries its DNA through intimate camera work and natural performances. The influence of Truffaut's The 400 Blows (1959) is evident in its portrayal of youth in crisis, while its political consciousness recalls Godard's La Chinoise (1967). Modern French directors like Céline Sciamma continue this tradition, as seen in Portrait of a Lady on Fire (2019).
